newsitem.title: ITALY: Chronology of the recent war against Italy's Mafia.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of the recent war against Italy's Mafia.

text.p: Following is a chronology of recent attacks by the Mafia and high-profile arrests before the detention on Friday of Pietro Aglieri.

1992 - Anti-Mafia magistrate Giovanni Falcone was killed in May by a bomb planted on a motorway near Palermo. Falcone's wife and three bodyguards also died. Two months later, a car bomb killed another anti-mafia crusader, magistrate Paolo Borsellino.
1993 - A crackdown on the mob leads to the arrest in January of "boss of bosses" Salvatore "Toto" Riina. The Corleonesi clan leader had been on the run for 23 years.
In May the Mafia hit back with an attack on Florence's famous Uffizi gallery which killed five and destroyed priceless works of art. Other bombs were set off in Rome and Milan.
In November Aglieri was almost captured after a car chase through Palermo.
1995, July - Italian police captured Riina's brother-in-law and right-hand man, Leoluca Bagarella.
1996, May - Giovanni Brusca, a top leader of the Mafia since Riina's capture, arrested in southern Sicily.

Brusca, in his late 30s, has admitted to pressing the button which blew up Falcone in 1992. A Mafia turncoat has also alleged that Brusca personally strangled an 11-year-old boy in 1995 and dissolved his body in a bath of acid.
1997, June - Arrest of Aglieri, one of the most powerful of the fugitive Mafia bosses. He has been indicted for the Falcone and Borsellino killings.
Investigators will now focus their attention on the outstanding name on the list of top Mafiosi still at large, Bernardo Provenzano.

The 62-year-old has been on the run for more than 25 years. Like Riina, with whom he grew up in Corleone, a hilltop town immortalised in Hollywood's "The Godfather" movies, Provenzano has been charged with Falcone's killing.
